events.title: Leo VIII claims the papacy with the backing of Otto I
events.description: Leo VIII, a Roman prelate appointed by Emperor Otto I, was ordained a bishop and claimed the Holy See in opposition to John XII. The Catholic Church counts him an antipope until 23 June 964 and the legitimate pope thereafter.
events.html: Leo VIII, a Roman prelate appointed by Emperor Otto I, was ordained a bishop and claimed the Holy See in opposition to John XII. The Catholic Church counts him an antipope until 23 June 964 and the legitimate pope thereafter.

events.title: Béla I is crowned king of Hungary at Székesfehérvár
events.description: Béla I, who had rebelled with Polish help when his brother Andrew I named his infant son Solomon as heir, was crowned at Székesfehérvár, the coronation place of Hungarian kings. He reigned until his death in 1063.

events.title: The Mongols sack Kiev
events.description: Batu Khan's army stormed Kiev after a siege, massacring much of the population. A traveller passing a few years later reported barely 200 houses standing; the city's ruin ended Kievan Rus as a power.
events.html: Batu Khan's army stormed Kiev after a siege, massacring much of the population. A traveller passing a few years later reported barely 200 houses standing; the city's ruin ended Kievan Rus as a power.

events.title: Christopher Columbus lands on Hispaniola
events.description: Christopher Columbus, who had mistaken Cuba for Japan, landed on Hispaniola at a bay he named San Nicolas, in present-day Haiti, and was welcomed by the Taíno. The island became the first base of Spanish colonisation in the Americas.
events.html: Christopher Columbus, who had mistaken Cuba for Japan, landed on Hispaniola at a bay he named San Nicolas, in present-day Haiti, and was welcomed by the Taíno. The island became the first base of Spanish colonisation in the Americas.

events.title: Spanish conquistadors found San Francisco de Quito
events.description: Sebastián de Benalcázar's men founded the Spanish city of Quito on the site of an Inca centre in the Andes. Its historic centre is today one of the best-preserved colonial cities in the Americas.
events.html: Sebastián de Benalcázar's men founded the Spanish city of Quito on the site of an Inca centre in the Andes. Its historic centre is today one of the best-preserved colonial cities in the Americas.

events.title: The Jacobite army turns back at Derby
events.description: Overruling Charles Edward Stuart, his commanders began a retreat from Derby, about 125 miles from London. The rising ended at Culloden in April 1746.
events.html: Overruling Charles Edward Stuart, his commanders began a retreat from Derby, about 125 miles from London. The rising ended at Culloden in April 1746.

events.title: Edison records and plays back 'Mary Had a Little Lamb'
events.description: Thomas Edison spoke the nursery rhyme into his tinfoil phonograph and heard his voice played back. It was the first time a machine had reproduced recorded human speech.
events.html: Thomas Edison spoke the nursery rhyme into his tinfoil phonograph and heard his voice played back. It was the first time a machine had reproduced recorded human speech.

events.title: Finland declares independence
events.description: The Finnish parliament adopted a declaration of independence from Russia, a month after the Bolshevik seizure of power. Lenin's government recognised it at the end of the month.
events.html: The Finnish parliament adopted a declaration of independence from Russia, a month after the Bolshevik seizure of power. Lenin's government recognised it at the end of the month.

events.title: The Anglo-Irish Treaty is signed
events.description: Irish and British delegates signed a treaty in London creating the Irish Free State as a dominion, with Northern Ireland able to opt out. Divisions over it led to the Irish Civil War.
